results.title: Operando spectroscopy - Wikipedia
results.content: **Operando spectroscopy** is an analytical methodology wherein the spectroscopic characterization of materials undergoing reaction is coupled *simultaneously* with measurement of catalytic activity and selectivity. In the context of organometallic catalysis, an *in situ* reaction involves the real-time measurement of a catalytic process using techniques such as mass spectrometry, NMR, infrared spectroscopy, and gas chromatography to help gain insight into functionality of the catalyst. *Operando* (Latin for *working*) spectroscopy refers to continuous spectra collection of a working catalyst, allowing for simultaneous evaluation of both structure and activity/selectivity of the catalyst. Operando spectroscopy requires measurement of the catalyst under (ideally) real *working conditions*, involving comparable temperature and pressure environments to those of industrially catalyzed reactions, but with a spectroscopic device inserted into the reaction vessel. Continuing development of operando reaction-cell design is in line with working towards minimizing the need for compromise between optimal catalysis conditions and spectroscopy. Raman spectroscopy is one of the easiest methods to integrate into a heterogeneous operando experiment, as these reactions typically occur in the gas phase, so there is very low litter interference and good data can be obtained for the species on the catalytic surface.*[clarification needed*] In order to use Raman, all that is required is to insert a small probe containing two optical fibers for excitation and detection. Operando confocal Raman micro-spectroscopy has been applied to the study of fuel cell catalytic layers with flowing reactant streams and controlled temperature. X-ray spectroscopy methods can be used for genuine operando analyses of catalysts and other functional materials. Ni is a typical catalyst material for the anode in high temperature SOFCs. The operando spectro-electrochemical cell for this high temperature gas-solid reaction study under electrochemical conditions was based on a typical high temperature heterogeneous catalysis cell, which was further equipped with electric terminals. results.title: Study of the surface species of CePr-supported Cu, Ni and CuNi catalysts at different Water Gas Shift reaction conditions - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Research article Study of the surface species of CePr-supported Cu, Ni and CuNi catalysts at different Water Gas Shift reaction conditions. The catalytic performance for Water Gas Shift Reaction and surface species at reaction conditions were studied by operando-DRIFTS of the bare Pr-promoted Ce oxide support, two supported monometallic Cu and Ni, and a bimetallic CuNi catalyst. To overcome these difficulties different formulations of catalysts were studied, involving a wide diversity of transition metals as active phases like Pt, Pd, Rh, Ru, Au, Ag, Cu, Ni, and Co, a relevant span of supports such as alumina, silica, ceria, activated carbon, basic oxides, and other rare-earth oxides. A series of Cu-Ni solids supported over ceria, promoted ceria, and activated carbon have been studied during the last 15 years as promising catalysts for the WGS reaction. The proper determination of the WGS reaction mechanism operating in the monometallic or bimetallic catalysts based on Cu or Ni over ceria has been explored by combining different techniques with relative success, in situ DRIFTS, XRD, EXAFS/XANES, and SSITKA [15]. In the present work, the bare support, Pr-promoted ceria, the monometallic Cu and Ni-based catalysts, and a bimetallic CuNi catalyst were studied by operando-DRIFTS with the aim of determining the influence of the active phase on the activity and selectivity towards WGS. The results obtained in this study highlight the complex interplay between active metals and the CePr support in determining the nature of surface intermediates and the prevailing mechanism in the Water Gas Shift (WGS) reaction. ### Effects of oxide supports on the water-gas shift reaction over PtNi bimetallic catalysts: Activity and methanation inhibition. ### Bimetallic Ni–Cu catalyst supported on CeO2 for high-temperature water–gas shift reaction: methane suppression via enhanced CO adsorption. ### Low-temperature water-gas shift reaction over Cu- and Ni-loaded cerium oxide catalysts. ### High-temperature water–gas shift reaction over Ni/xK/CeO2 catalysts: Suppression of methanation via formation of bridging carbonyls. ### Preferential CO oxidation in hydrogen (PROX) on ceria-supported catalysts, part I: oxidation state and surface species on Pt/CeO2 under reaction conditions. ### FTIR study of low-temperature water-gas shift reaction on gold/ceria catalyst. ### Mono and bimetallic Cu-Ni structured catalysts for the water gas shift reaction.
